items.title: Standard real and normalized complex Gaussian matrix laws
items.statement: Define the independent-entry real standard Gaussian and normalized complex Gaussian matrix laws, with complex entries (X+iY)/sqrt(2) and E|z|^2=1.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, §10.1
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, §§11.1, 11.4

items.title: Orthogonal-projector power error inequality
items.statement: For finite real or complex A, orthogonal projector P, and integer q>=0, ||(I-P)A||2 <= ||(I-P)(AA*)^q A||2^(1/(2q+1)).

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Proposition 8.6 and Theorem 9.2
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, Lemma 11.8

items.title: Exact Gaussian randomized range finder
items.statement: For fixed A and ell=k+p, draw an iid real standard or normalized complex Gaussian Omega, form Y=A Omega, take any orthonormal basis Q of Ran(Y), and return QQ* A and its actual rank.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, Algorithm 4.1
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, §11.1.1

items.title: Finite Gaussian increment comparison
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $N\ge1$ be an integer, and let $(X_i)_{i=1}^N$ and $(Y_i)_{i=1}^N$ be
finite centered real Gaussian families. If $\mathbb E(X_i-X_j)^2\le\mathbb E(Y_i-Y_j)^2$ for every
$i,j$, then $\mathbb E\max_iX_i\le\mathbb E\max_iY_i$.
Here a finite centered real Gaussian family means a finite real vector that
is a real-linear image of finitely many independent standard real Gaussian
scalars.

references.title: S. Chevet, Séries de variables aléatoires gaussiennes..., §2
Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, Proposition A.2

items.title: Orthogonal and unitary invariance of Gaussian matrix blocks
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $G\in F^{a\times b}$ have the iid Gaussian law of
[[def-standard-real-and-normalized-complex-gaussian-matrix-law]]. If $U,V$
are compatible orthogonal matrices for $F=\mathbb R$ or unitary matrices for
$F=\mathbb C$, then $U^*GV$ has the same iid law as $G$. In particular, if
$W\in F^{n\times n}$ is orthogonal/unitary and $\Omega\in F^{n\times\ell}$
is iid Gaussian, then any two disjoint row blocks of $W^*\Omega$ are
independent standard Gaussian matrices.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, §10.1
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, §11.4.2

items.title: Reorthogonalized randomized power subspace iteration
items.statement: For integer q>=0, draw Omega and alternate A* and A applications, replacing each sample block by an exact orthonormal basis of its range after every application; return the final basis.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, Algorithms 4.3–4.4
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, §11.6

items.title: Deterministic SVD-partition error bound for the range finder
items.statement: When the top k sketch block Omega1 has full row rank, ||(I-QQ*)A||2 <= sigma_(k+1)+||Sigma2 Omega2 Omega1†||2, including rank(A)<k.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, Theorem 9.1
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, Theorem 11.4

items.title: Real scaled-Gaussian spectral and Frobenius product bounds
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $a,r,s,b$ be positive integers, let $S\in\mathbb R^{a\times r}$ and $T\in\mathbb R^{s\times b}$ be fixed,
and let $G\in\mathbb R^{r\times s}$ have independent standard real Gaussian
entries. Then
$$\mathbb E\|SGT\|_F^2=\|S\|_F^2\|T\|_F^2,\qquad \mathbb E\|SGT\|_2\le\|S\|_2\|T\|_F+\|S\|_F\|T\|_2.$$
The spectral estimate in this lemma is real-field only.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, Proposition 10.1 and Appendix A.1
S. Chevet, Séries de variables aléatoires gaussiennes..., Lemma 3.1

items.title: A wide Gaussian matrix has full row rank almost surely
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $k\ge1$, $\ell>k$, and let $G\in F^{k\times\ell}$ have iid standard
real Gaussian or normalized complex Gaussian entries. Then
$\operatorname{rank}(G)=k$ almost surely.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, §10.2
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, §11.4.2

items.title: Exact Frobenius moments of wide Gaussian pseudoinverses
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $k\ge1$ and let $p$ be a positive integer, with $p\ge2$ over $\mathbb R$
and $p\ge1$ over normalized $\mathbb C$. Let $G\in F^{k\times(k+p)}$ have iid entries as in
[[def-standard-real-and-normalized-complex-gaussian-matrix-law]]. Then $G$
has full row rank almost surely and
$$\mathbb E\|G^\dagger\|_F^2= \begin{cases}k/(p-1),&F=\mathbb R,\\k/p,&F=\mathbb C.\end{cases}$$
The complex entry convention is variance one, $\mathbb E|G_{ij}|^2=1$. Write
$G^\dagger=G^+$ for the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of
[[def-moore-penrose-pseudoinverse]]. On the full-row-rank event,
$$G^\dagger=G^*(GG^*)^{-1},\qquad (G^\dagger)^*G^\dagger=(GG^*)^{-1}.$$
Here $U\sim\Gamma(a,\theta)$ means that $U$ has density
$u^{a-1}e^{-u/\theta}/(\theta^a\Gamma(a))$ for $u>0$. For every diagonal
index $i$, $((GG^*)^{-1})_{ii}$ has distribution $1/U$ with
$U\sim\Gamma((p+1)/2,2)$ over $\mathbb R$ and $U\sim\Gamma(p+1,1)$ over
$\mathbb C$.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, Proposition 10.2 and Appendix A.1
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, §11.4.2

items.title: Power-rangefinder error transfer under finite expected powered error
items.statement:
Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $(\Xi,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)$ be a
probability space, let $A\in F^{m\times n}$ be fixed, let $\ell\ge1$ be an
integer, and let $q\ge0$ be an integer. Let $\Omega:\Xi\to F^{n\times\ell}$
be measurable and let $P:\Xi\to F^{m\times m}$ be a measurable orthogonal
projector-valued map whose value $P(\xi)$ projects onto the output range of the procedure in
[[alg-randomized-power-subspace-iteration-with-qr]] applied to $A,\Omega(\xi),q$.
Assume
$$\mathbb E\|(I-P)(AA^*)^qA\|_2<\infty,$$
where expectation is with respect to $\mathbb P$. Then
$$\mathbb E\|(I-P)A\|_2\le \left(\mathbb E\|(I-P)(AA^*)^qA\|_2\right)^{1/(2q+1)}.$$
This is a transfer inequality; it assumes the powered error expectation has
already been bounded.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Theorem 9.2
Martinsson and Tropp, Lemma 11.8

items.title: Affine second-moment bounds for normalized complex Gaussian block products

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, §10.1 and Appendix A.1; standard Gaussian block context, with the present normalized-complex estimates derived locally
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, §11.4.2; real Gaussian rangefinder context, with the present normalized-complex estimates derived locally

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $k\ge1$, $p\ge2$, $\ell=k+p$, and $d,a\ge1$ be integers. Let
$G_1\in\mathbb C^{k\times\ell}$ and $G_2\in\mathbb C^{d\times\ell}$ be
independent matrices with iid normalized complex Gaussian entries as in
[[def-standard-real-and-normalized-complex-gaussian-matrix-law]], so
$\mathbb E|g|^2=1$. Put $Z=G_2G_1^\dagger$, where $G_1^\dagger$ is the
Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse of [[def-moore-penrose-pseudoinverse]]. For every
fixed $S\in\mathbb C^{a\times d}$, writing $C=2\sqrt2e$ with
$e=\exp(1)$ as in [[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]], one has
$$\mathbb E\|SZ\|_2^2\le\frac{C\ell}{p^2}\left(\|S\|_F^2+\frac p4\|S\|_2^2\right),$$
$$\mathbb E\|SZ\|_2^2\le\frac{e^2\ell}{p^2}\left(\|S\|_F^2+\frac p2\|S\|_2^2\right).$$
Here $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the induced operator norm of
[[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]] and
$\|\cdot\|_F$ is the Frobenius norm of [[def-frobenius-matrix-norm]]. These
are coarse second-moment bounds; no sharp complex Chevet comparison is assumed.
The values on the null event where $G_1$ loses row rank may be set to zero in
these integrals.

items.title: Spectral moments and integrable tails for wide Gaussian pseudoinverses
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
For $G\in F^{k\times(k+p)}$ as in
[[lem-wide-gaussian-pseudoinverse-frobenius-moments]], put $X=\|G^\dagger\|_2$.
For $0<q<(p+1)/2$ over $\mathbb R$ and $0<q<p+1$ over normalized $\mathbb C$,
$$\mathbb E X^{2q}\le C_R(q):=\frac{2^{-q}\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma((p+1)/2-q)\Gamma(k/2+q)}{\Gamma((p+1)/2)\Gamma(k/2)\Gamma(q+1/2)},$$
$$\mathbb E X^{2q}\le C_C(q):=\frac{\Gamma(p+1-q)\Gamma(k+q)}{\Gamma(p+1)\Gamma(k)\Gamma(q+1)}.$$
For integers $p\ge2$, writing $\ell=k+p$ and $a=e\sqrt\ell/p$,
$$\mathbb E X^p\le a^p\quad(F=\mathbb R),\qquad \mathbb E X^{2p}\le a^{2p}\quad(F=\mathbb C).$$
Consequently $\mathbb E X\le a$ and
$$\mathbb P\{X>t\}\le\min(1,(a/t)^p)\quad(F=\mathbb R),\qquad \mathbb P\{X>t\}\le\min(1,(a/t)^{2p})\quad(F=\mathbb C),$$
for $t>0$. In the randomized range-finder application $p\ge2$, so these tails
are integrable at infinity.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, Proposition 10.2 and Appendix A.1
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, §11.4.2

items.title: Direct expected spectral bound for the normalized complex range finder

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, §§9.1–10.2; the present normalized-complex moment and rank-shift argument is derived locally
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, §§11.4.1–11.4.2; the present normalized-complex proof is derived locally

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $A\in\mathbb C^{m\times n}$ be fixed, let $k\ge2$, $p\ge2$ be integers
with $\ell=k+p\le\min(m,n)$, and draw $\Omega\in\mathbb C^{n\times\ell}$
with iid normalized complex Gaussian entries satisfying $\mathbb E|g|^2=1$.
Let $Q$ be the exact finite-scan range-finder basis of
$\operatorname{Ran}(A\Omega)$ returned by
[[alg-gaussian-randomized-range-finder]], and put $P=QQ^*$. Then
$$\mathbb E\|(I-P)A\|_2\le\sqrt{\frac{\ell}{p}}\,\sigma_{k+1} +\frac{e\sqrt\ell}{p}\left(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
In particular, the original approved bound with leading coefficient
$1+\sqrt{k/(p-1)}$ follows. The algorithm and sketch width $\ell$ are
unchanged; only the analysis may use a larger SVD partition rank.

items.title: Expected spectral error of the real Gaussian range finder
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability
measure. Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ be fixed, $k\ge2$, $p\ge2$,
$\ell=k+p\le\min(m,n)$, and draw $\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times\ell}$ with
iid standard real Gaussian entries. If $Q$ is an orthonormal basis for
$\operatorname{Ran}(A\Omega)$, then
$$\mathbb E\|A-QQ^*A\|_2\le \left(1+\sqrt{\frac{k}{p-1}}\right)\sigma_{k+1} +\frac{e\sqrt{k+p}}{p}\left(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
The rank of $Q$ may be smaller than $\ell$; exact arithmetic is assumed.
The comparator $\sigma_{k+1}$ is the minimum spectral error among all
rank-at-most-$k$ approximations.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, Theorem 10.6 and its proof
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, Theorem 11.5

items.title: Expected spectral error for real and normalized complex Gaussian range finders
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $A\in F^{m\times n}$ be fixed, where $F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$. Let
$k\ge2$, $p\ge2$, $\ell=k+p\le\min(m,n)$, and draw $\Omega$ with iid
standard real entries if $F=\mathbb R$ or normalized complex entries if
$F=\mathbb C$. If $Q$ is an orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{Ran}(A\Omega)$,
then
$$\mathbb E\|A-QQ^*A\|_2\le \left(1+\sqrt{\frac{k}{p-1}}\right)\sigma_{k+1} +\frac{e\sqrt{k+p}}{p}\left(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
This preserves the normalized-complex convention $\mathbb E|\Omega_{ij}|^2=1$.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Theorem 10.6 and its complex-case discussion
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, Theorem 11.5

items.title: Expected real Gaussian power-rangefinder error
items.statement:
Under the real-field hypotheses of
[[thm-real-gaussian-rangefinder-expected-spectral-error]], let $q\ge0$ be an
integer, draw the same Gaussian sketch $\Omega$, and let $Q$ be the basis
returned by [[alg-randomized-power-subspace-iteration-with-qr]] on $A,\Omega,q$.
Equivalently, if $B=(AA^*)^qA$, then $\operatorname{Ran}(Q)=\operatorname{Ran}(B\Omega)$. Then
$$\mathbb E\|(I-QQ^*)A\|_2\le \left[ \left(1+\sqrt{\frac{k}{p-1}}\right)\sigma_{k+1}^{2q+1} +\frac{e\sqrt{k+p}}{p} \left(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^{2(2q+1)}\right)^{1/2} \right]^{1/(2q+1)}.$$

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Corollary 10.10
Martinsson and Tropp, Corollary 11.9

items.title: Expected real and normalized complex Gaussian power-rangefinder error
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $A\in F^{m\times n}$, $F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, with the same
$k\ge2$, $p\ge2$, $\ell=k+p\le\min(m,n)$ and field-normalized Gaussian
draws as in [[thm-gaussian-rangefinder-expected-spectral-error]]. For an
integer $q\ge0$, let $Q$ be the basis returned by
[[alg-randomized-power-subspace-iteration-with-qr]] on $A,\Omega,q$. Equivalently,
for $B=(AA^*)^qA$, $\operatorname{Ran}(Q)=\operatorname{Ran}(B\Omega)$. The corresponding
singular-value bound
$$\mathbb E\|(I-QQ^*)A\|_2\le \left[ \left(1+\sqrt{\frac{k}{p-1}}\right)\sigma_{k+1}^{2q+1} +\frac{e\sqrt{k+p}}{p} \left(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^{2(2q+1)}\right)^{1/2} \right]^{1/(2q+1)}.$$

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Corollary 10.10
Martinsson and Tropp, Corollary 11.9

items.title: Exact range recovery on a rank-k matrix
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability law.
Let $A=\operatorname{diag}(4,1,0,0)\in\mathbb R^{4\times4}$, take target
rank $k=2$, oversampling $p=2$, and draw $\Omega\in\mathbb R^{4\times4}$
with iid standard real Gaussian entries. The randomized range finder returns
$QQ^*A=A$ almost surely, so its spectral error is zero.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Finding Structure with Randomness, §10.2
Martinsson and Tropp, Randomized Numerical Linear Algebra: Foundations & Algorithms, §11.4.2

items.title: A small mode is lost by an unorthogonalized power pass
items.statement: In an explicit thresholded dyadic arithmetic model, unorthogonalized powering drops a small singular mode while QR between multiplications preserves it.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Algorithm 4.4 and Remark 4.3
Martinsson and Tropp, §11.6

items.title: A slowly decaying singular tail makes the Frobenius term dominate
items.statement: For sigma_j=j^(-1/2), the tail-Frobenius contribution in the real expected range-finder bound eventually dominates the sigma_(k+1) contribution for fixed k,p.

references.title: Halko, Martinsson, and Tropp, Theorem 10.6 and discussion after it
Martinsson and Tropp, Theorem 11.5 and discussion after it
